subject: Pricing stability carve-out / proposed annualized true-up (redlines)
messages:
From: Kerri Nguyen <kerri@stratusai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@stratusai.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing stability carve-out — ask on annualized floor smoothing

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed. Before we can route the order form internally we have one substantive ask on the Pricing Exhibit: Stratus is requesting a temporary "stability carve-out" to address unpredictable burst usage during our pilot. Specifically:

- Replace the hard monthly minimum (Section 2, Pricing Exhibit) with an annualized smoothing true-up (rolling 90-day average applied monthly, with a 6-month lookback).
- Add a one-time "pilot protection" credit equal to 15% of underage against the first two quarters if monthly spend falls below the proposed annualized floor.
- Request language that caps aggregate credits at a fixed dollar cap (to protect Redwood economics).

We recognize this is non-standard; happy to mark it as a limited-duration pilot amendment (6 months) and include a sunset. Can your team propose language or redlines for the Pricing Exhibit?

Attached current OrderForm_v3 and our procurement template for reference.

-Kerri

Kerri Nguyen
Head of Procurement, StratusAI
kerri@stratusai.com
[Attachment: OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF, 456KB)]
[Attachment: Stratus_Procurement_Template.docx (DOCX, 120KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kerri Nguyen <kerri@stratusai.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@stratusai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing stability carve-out — ask on annualized floor smoothing

Kerri — appreciate the transparency and the pilot framing. High level response: we can be flexible but need to protect the platform economics and set clear guardrails. Proposed principles from our side:

- Preferred: rolling 90-day average true-up but with a "soft floor" (i.e., credits don’t become payable until underage exceeds 10% in any quarter).
- Credits: ok to offer a declining pilot protection credit (15% first quarter, 10% second quarter) subject to an aggregate cap (suggest $50k).
- Sunset: 6-month pilot with an automatic reversion to standard monthly minimum unless both parties agree in writing.

I’m looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (revops/pricing) to propose concrete redline text for the Pricing Exhibit and the order form. Marissa/Karthik — can you review and suggest language that preserves our right to true-up while giving them a path to trial?

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
[Attachment: PricingExhibit_DRAFT.docx (DOCX, 210KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kerri Nguyen <kerri@stratusai.com>, Samir Patel <samir@stratusai.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing stability carve-out — proposed redlines attached

Jonas / Karthik — I reviewed Kerri's request and drafted a set of redlines that aim to balance the ask with clear limits. Key points in the redline (attached):

- Section 2.1: Replace permanent monthly minimum with an "Annualized Smoothing True-Up" definition. Text clarifies calculation: rolling 90-day average, applied monthly, with a 6-month review window.
- Section 2.3: Introduce "Pilot Protection Credit" limited to two consecutive quarters: 15% credit (Q1) then 10% (Q2). Credits are applied to invoices but are non-refundable and do not create a recurring liability.
- Section 2.4: Aggregate Credit Cap: fixed-dollar cap set at $45,000. This cap is intended to protect Redwood from disproportionate credit exposure.
- Section 2.6: Sunset & Evaluation: pilot automatically expires after six months, at which point the parties will either transition to standard pricing or execute a written amendment.

I also included a short clause requiring Stratus to provide monthly usage reports and a single point of contact for consumption disputes. Please review the attached PricingExhibit_DRAFT.docx redline and advise if you want me to send this back to Kerri as tracked changes or as marked-up bullets.

Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: PricingExhibit_DRAFT_redline.docx (DOCX, 218KB)]

From: Samir Patel <samir@stratusai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kerri Nguyen <kerri@stratusai.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing stability carve-out — proposed redlines attached

Thanks Jonas / Marissa — that looks reasonable and much closer to what procurement can approve. A couple quick items from our side:

- Can we increase the aggregate credit cap to $60k? Our CFO asks for extra cushion given forecast uncertainty.
- We accept the 6-month sunset but would like a 30-day notice period before automatic reversion so we have time to plan.

If Redwood can accept the $60k cap and add a 30-day notice window, procurement will route this for signature this week. Otherwise we can sign with the $45k cap and evaluate after Q1.

Once we have agreement on those two points, can you send a final PDF for signature (DocuSign link preferred)?

Appreciate the collaboration — excited to get started.

-Samir

Samir Patel
VP Product, StratusAI
samir@stratusai.com
